correctness.rationale: Normalize \(r=\beta/\alpha\). Proposition 1 gives the universal upper bound \(1\); for \(r\le1\), triangle and reverse-triangle inequalities give the sharper \(2r\) bound. Two explicit unit Birkhoff-orthogonal pairs attain \(2r\) for \(0<r\le1/2\) and \(1\) for \(r\ge1/2\). The Birkhoff conditions are checked directly for every real \(\lambda\). For the theorem-2 comparison, any boundary segment of the square lies in one face; a shared saturated coordinate then has magnitude \(|1-2/r|>1\) at the second required endpoint whenever \(r<1\). Thus the exact formula and the entire counterexample interval are proved without finite-experiment inference.

value.rationale: The square plane is a canonical extremal Banach space, and the result determines the new skew constant for every positive parameter rather than on an arbitrary slice. The exact transition \(\beta/\alpha=1/2\) is structurally meaningful: it is also where a fixed face-supported Birkhoff pair begins saturating the universal bound. The interval \(1/2\le\beta/\alpha<1\) exposes a concrete failure of a published iff criterion and pinpoints why flat-face geometry matters, making the fact useful as a benchmark for subsequent skew-orthogonality constants and equality analyses.
